**STAGE 2 BUILD READY FOR REVIEW — cc/stage-2-vision-pixel-2026-07-21 (do not merge until Cowork clears)**

Branch advanced this run — new commit `4f878f36` on branch `cc/stage-2-vision-pixel-2026-07-21` (parent = the Stage-2 privacy tip `d7d06617`).
Branch-only. No main write, no merge, no deploy, no publish, no external send, no payment, no account creation.

- **What was actually missing:** the spec's "redact obvious PII/secrets in images **before any cloud call**" was still only half done. Last run closed the *metadata* half (EXIF/GPS/IPTC/PNG text). The *pixel* half was explicitly unbuilt and honestly disclaimed — an email address visible on screen still went to the paid model. This run closes it, with the user in the loop rather than with fake auto-detection.
- **New `netlify/functions/lib/vision-pixel-redact.mjs`** (267 lines, zero deps — `node:zlib` only): a real PNG codec (chunk walk, inflate, per-row unfilter incl. Paeth, paint, re-filter, deflate, CRC32 rebuild). Regions arrive as 0..1 fractions, are clamped to the image, and are painted **opaque black into the pixel data**. Verified by decoding the output: covered pixels are *destroyed*, not overlaid — a full-image redaction leaves no original pixel value anywhere in the buffer. Re-encoding also drops every ancillary chunk by construction.
- **Refusals are real, and never hand back sendable bytes:** JPEG → `format-not-pixel-redactable` (no DCT re-encode here — say so, don't fake it); palette / 16-bit / interlaced PNG → `unsupported-png-*`; malformed PNG, garbage coordinates, zero-area boxes → refused. On every refusal there is no `base64` key at all, so a caller physically cannot ship the original by accident.
- **Handler wired in the right order:** metadata scrub → **pixel paint** → paid call. If the user *asked* for redaction and we cannot deliver it, the request **aborts** with `reason:'pixel-redaction-failed'` and an honest fallback — shipping the unpainted original to a third-party model after being asked to mask it would be the worst possible failure mode, so it cannot happen.
- **Surface (this is what makes it reachable):** the consent dialog in the web widget now shows the image on a canvas with **drag-to-paint**, undo, clear, and a live count. On submit the canvas is flattened to PNG **in the browser**, so with a painted region the original never leaves the machine at all — and the regions are *also* sent so the server repaints them. Belt and braces. Sentinel's vendored copy re-synced byte-identical (the no-drift guard caught it, as designed).
- **Rule 14 wording, enforced by tests, not by good intentions:** with **zero** regions painted, every disclosure still says the image goes **UNREDACTED** and the word "painted" never appears. With N painted, it says exactly N, says the pixels are *destroyed not covered*, and still says **every pixel you did not paint is sent UNREDACTED** — plus "nothing is found or masked automatically, there is no OCR." The receipt in the UI is real-or-silent: it renders only from the server's confirmed `pixelRedaction.ok`. **Automatic pixel PII detection remains NOT built and is not claimed anywhere.**
- **Tests:** new `tests/vision-pixel-redact.test.mjs` (11 tests) registered in `npm run vision:test`. Full suite **verified clean-room from a `git archive` of `4f878f36`** on node v22.22.3:

**Source of record:** `aria-vault/01_Frontal/IIS/Strategy-15-Years-Ahead.md` → PART 3e → DELTA 2026-07-28 (every claim below carries a source URL there; Rule 14 — if a stat loses its URL, cut the stat).

### What changed out there
1. **Four NEW publishers now own the Toronto managed-IT answer slot** we target with `managed-it-cost-toronto.html`: BALANCED+ (balanced.plus), CloudSecureTech, eITcare, AITS — plus Clutch's live-dated Toronto MSP ranking. None are new MSP competitors; all are new *citation* competitors.
2. **Fusion Computing published a dedicated M365 Copilot-oversharing SMB audit article.** The content half of our 07-14 wedge is closed. We still own the only free client-side *tool* — that is now the entire differentiator.
3. **Per-resolution AI pricing became the industry default, with public street prices:** eesel ~$0.40 · HubSpot Customer Agent $0.50 (dropped April 2026) · Intercom $0.99 · Zendesk $1.50 committed / $2.00 PAYG. Analysts now forecast MSPs moving to outcome-based pricing (uptime/MTTR/security) in 2026.
4. **Atera Robin hardened its proof machine** (rename from IT Autopilot, Salesforce integration, "Ticket flow breakdown" resolution analytics, named-customer public proof) with the 50%-in-90-days-or-fees-waived guarantee intact.
5. **AEO mechanics moved against own-page-only strategies:** Google top-10 ↔ AI-citation overlap fell ~75% → 17–38%; organic CTR −61% where an AI Overview appears; referral traffic −52% since Jul-2024; Reddit citations +87%; top-3 domains hold 22% of all citations.
6. **Forrester: 40–60% of IT triage/repetitive remediation automated in 2026.** Counter-signal: ChannelPro/ITPro — reselling AI is not where MSP margin lives; governing it is.

### Why it matters
Two clocks are now running. (i) Fusion is publishing into our Copilot wedge — the tool must out-run the article. (ii) With a public $0.40–$2.00 street price for one AI-resolved ticket sitting next to a $120–$250/user/mo flat GTA plan, **any buyer can now do that arithmetic, and no GTA MSP has published the honest version of it.** The §3e white space (endpoint action + audit-chained honest metrics + founder white-glove at SMB price) still holds — but the citation half of §3d has shifted off our own pages and onto third-party surfaces we can only reach through Ahmad's account-creation clicks.

Handler now issues `diagnosisId` + `feedbackEndpoint` on **both** answer paths; **abstains are rateable too** (a wrong abstain is the cheapest, highest-value input to the KB growth factory).

## 2026-07-29T01:57Z — CC (Cowork) · STAGE 2 BUILD READY FOR REVIEW — cc/stage-2-vision-pdf-2026-07-28 (do not merge until Cowork clears)

**STAGE 2 BUILD READY FOR REVIEW — cc/stage-2-vision-pdf-2026-07-28 (do not merge until Cowork clears)**

- **Feature code this run.** Re-reading the spec's input list against the widget found the third declared input unreachable: the spec says **"image/log/PDF"** and the endpoint has accepted `kind:'pdf'` since run 1, but **dropping a PDF on any of the three surfaces hit "that file type isn't supported yet."** Same class of defect as last run's discarded feedback vote — the API claims a capability the product does not have. Built.
- **New `assets/aria-pdf-text.js`** (+ byte-identical Sentinel vendor copy): dependency-free PDF text extraction. **No pdf.js, no CDN, no npm package, no paid API, no server round-trip** — FlateDecode via the native `DecompressionStream` (browsers and Node 18+ both have it), so it is **$0 forever and works offline**. Handles uncompressed + Flate streams, literal/hex strings, `Tj`/`TJ`/`'`/`"`, TJ kerning re-spaced into word gaps, UTF-16BE + WinAnsi, and damaged/absent xref tables.
- **PRIVACY:** the PDF is read **on the device** — the file itself is **never uploaded**, only the extracted text, and that goes down the existing server-side offline-KB path (no third-party AI model) where the existing PII redaction already applies. The extractor has **no fetch/XHR/WebSocket/sendBeacon at all** and a test asserts that, so the UI's promise cannot drift from the code.
- **Rule 14:** a scan is a picture of text and a custom font encoding decodes to plausible garbage — either would feed the diagnoser noise wearing the user's error as a costume. So it refuses: `encrypted-pdf`, `no-text-layer`, `unsupported-pdf-encoding`, `text-not-recoverable` (explicit printable-character quality bar), `pdf-too-large`, `not-a-pdf`. **Every refusal returns `text:''`** so a caller cannot ship it anyway, and the widget shows the reason + "screenshot the page with the error" instead.
- **Rule 15:** additive only — image, paste, log and screen-capture paths untouched; Sentinel vendor copy byte-identical (test-enforced).
- **Tests re-run first-hand from the COMMITTED objects** (clean `git archive` tree): 51 + 17 + 60 + 33 + 9 + 11 + 13 + **15 new** → **0 failures**, `vision:test` exit 0. The new suite builds **real PDF bytes**, not a mock of our own parser. `forums-mvp` / `forums-commons` / `concierge-service` green after the script-tag additions.
- **End-to-end spot check (real path):** Flate PDF containing *"Windows cannot connect to the printer … error 0x0000011b"* + an email + a phone → extracted locally → email/phone redacted → matched **`l1-printer-001-not-printing`, confidence 41 (high)** against the real 281-chunk KB.
- **Honest notes:** four of my own first-cut assertions/behaviours were wrong (TJ kerning, an MB figure using 1e6, unobserved writer-promise rejections, an incomplete archive extraction) — all recorded in ADDENDUM 24, not hidden. Pushing into the mount repo printed the known `objects/incoming-*` unlink warnings; the objects landed (branch resolves) but the temp dirs could not be cleaned. **Full 28-suite Rule-16 sweep NOT re-run** — sandbox disk ~1.9 GB free; 10 files touched, and the three non-vision suites that read the edited HTML were re-run.
- **Blockers unchanged:** no GitHub credential in sandbox (push staged). `ARIA_VISION_MODEL` + `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` stay Ahmad's deploy one-click — **the PDF path is $0 and works today without them.**

## 2026-07-29 — STAGE 2 (Series 2) — log triage slice landed, branch-only

**STAGE 2 BUILD READY FOR REVIEW — cc/stage-2-vision-log-2026-07-29 (do not merge until Cowork clears)**

Isolated branch off the Stage-2 lineage tip (`cc/stage-2-vision-pdf-2026-07-28`). NOT merged, NOT
deployed, main untouched. Kept on its own branch so it cannot collide with the Series-1 flywheel's
merges.

**What this run fixed.** A dropped `.log` / Event Viewer export was being read like a pasted
sentence — first ~4000 characters to the retriever. Real logs put a header and hundreds of routine
Information rows there, so on a realistic Windows Event Log CSV the old path confidently returned
"Windows 7 still running" (score 406) while the actual fault — a print-spooler plug-in failure
repeated 42× plus an unclean-reboot bugcheck — sat further down the file, unread. A confident wrong
answer is precisely what Rule 14 exists to stop.

**Landed**
- `netlify/functions/lib/vision-log-triage.mjs` (new; pure, offline, $0, zero network): format
  detection, severity classification, signature collapsing (42 repeats → one finding, count 42),
  two-stage ranking (severity tier is HARD — every critical outranks every error — then
  repetition/recency within tier), success-noise demotion, and event-ID / hex / bugcheck /
  exception / provider extraction. The retriever now sees only verbatim failure lines + signals.
- Two new honest abstains: a log with no failure lines (`log-no-failure-lines`) and a log we cannot
  read as text (`log-binary-not-text`). A clean log is no longer "diagnosed".
- Widget (web + vendored Sentinel copy, byte-identical): collapsible **"What I read in your log"**
  evidence panel — verbatim lines, severity, repeat counts, line numbers — so the user can check
  our reasoning rather than trust it.
- Triage summary now goes through the same redactor as the findings (the existing handler test
  caught a raw token reaching the summary field — real catch, fixed).

**Tests.** 23 new (`tests/vision-log-triage.test.mjs`) covering buried-fault retrieval, exact repeat
counts, verbatim-only findings, real line numbers, severity-over-volume, clean-log abstain,
binary-log abstain, end-to-end correctness vs the old raw path, PII redaction, and a 220k-line
scale/latency bound. `tests/vision-feedback.test.mjs` [12] generalised from "exactly 2 answer paths"
to "every answer path is rateable" — the frozen count would have failed a correct change.

**Sweep:** all 23 vision + site test files green. `tests/forums-concierge.test.mjs` fails identically
WITHOUT this change (missing `@netlify/blobs` in the build environment) — pre-existing, unrelated,
not introduced here.

**Honest limitations of this run**
- Could not `git push` to origin — no GitHub credentials in the build environment. The branch was
  pushed into the local repo instead and is present as `cc/stage-2-vision-log-2026-07-29`. A
  portable bundle is at `outputs/stage-2-vision-log-triage-2026-07-29.bundle`.
- Fast-forwarding `cc/stage-2-vision-2026-07` to this work was rejected by the filesystem
  (ref update permission). The work lives on the dated branch above, matching the lineage naming.
- No live review yet: Cowork still reviews with real screenshots and a real Event Viewer export
  before any merge.

### 2026-07-29 - CC (Stage-2 vision lane, parallel) - STAGE 2 BUILD READY FOR REVIEW

**STAGE 2 BUILD READY FOR REVIEW — `cc/stage-2-vision-fix-2026-07-29` (do not merge until Cowork clears)**

Tip `a46763c4`, parent `9c41d663` (the handoff tip Cowork cleared in flywheel run 140). Branch-only:
no main write, no merge, no deploy, no publish, no external send, no payment, no spend. Nothing in
the Series-1 flywheel's file set was touched.

**What this run closed.** The spec's payoff is "correct diagnosis + a working one-click fix". The
diagnosis has been real for several runs; the fix was a button. `Fix this with ARIA` had two
behaviours — a host-supplied `onFix` (ARIA web deep-links into Sentinel, Sentinel runs its own
gated resolve; both worked), or, for everyone else, `location.href = '/aria?fix=<recipeId>'`.
Nothing on this site has ever read a `?fix=` parameter. "Everyone else" meant the Forums Ask-AI
tab, which the spec names as a first-class surface: drop a screenshot, get a correct diagnosis,
press the fix button, land on /aria with the diagnosis, the recipe and the reason for the visit all
gone. Same defect class as the dead `?escalate=1`, the discarded feedback vote, and the PDF the API
accepted but no surface could produce.

**Landed**
- `netlify/functions/lib/vision-fix-plan.mjs` (new; pure, offline, $0, zero network): composes a
  reviewable plan from the vetted recipe library. Steps verbatim and in order — nothing invented.
  A step `aria-guided-fix` would refuse to sign (red/black) has its command WITHHELD with the
  reason stated, and the withheld list is asserted against what the endpoint actually refuses, so
  drift cannot quietly offer an unsignable click. An unknown recipe returns a refusal, never an
  improvised fix. `notRun: true` is stamped on every plan and enforced on both sides of the
  transfer, so no surface can render a plan as an outcome.
- `assets/aria-vision-fix-handoff.js` (new, + byte-identical Sentinel vendor copy): the transfer
  half. sessionStorage, never the URL; consumed once and cleared; refuses data: URLs, base64 blobs
  and control bytes on the way in and on the way out; no fetch, no eval, no exec.

## 2026-08-04 - STAGE 2 VISION BUILD (Series 2, parallel, branch-only)

**STAGE 2 BUILD READY FOR REVIEW - cc/stage-2-vision-cache-2026-08-04 (do not merge until Cowork clears)**

Slice this run: the last unbuilt clause of the spec's cost line - "gate cloud-vision calls behind
real use + prompt-cache". The prompt cache only discounts the SYSTEM block; the image tokens were
billed in full on EVERY call, including calls that re-answered a question we already answered
(feedback "Not yet" retries, flaky-connection retries, the same photo on web then Sentinel, the
same dialog in ARIA then Forums). Each of those also burned a unit of the visitor's free allowance
for an answer we already had.

- New: `netlify/functions/lib/vision-result-cache.mjs` (pure, offline, $0, no network, no disk,
  node:crypto only). Keyed on the exact bytes we were about to send + media type + model id +
  a bumpable PROMPT_VERSION. TTL (6h) AND a hard entry cap (200), oldest-first eviction refreshed
  on read. Kill-switch whose typo case leaves the cost control ON.
- Wired into `aria-vision-diagnose.mjs` AFTER the metadata scrub and pixel redaction (we key what
  would actually leave the machine) and BEFORE the paid call. A hit skips the wire call, the spend
  log, and the allowance unit. Storage happens only after runVision succeeds.
- The allowance refusal is now DEFERRED and fires only on a cache MISS - refusing an answer that
  costs nothing would punish the visitor with a cost control instead of protecting them with it.
  The global ceiling is unchanged and still enforced.
- Widget (web + byte-identical Sentinel vendor copy) names the age of the reading and says outright
  that we did not look again, no new cloud call was made, and it used none of the free allowance.

Rule 14: only a successful, already-redacted description is stored - an abstain can never be
replayed as a diagnosis. A cached string is not re-scored (asserted: same confidence as the fresh
call). A different model or bumped prompt cannot reach a prior entry. Every hit is disclosed.
Privacy: the image is never stored, only a SHA-256 of it; no visitor identifier is attached.

Named behaviour change (not hidden): the privacy pre-flight now runs before the allowance decision,
so an unreadable image is refused for BEING UNREADABLE rather than for allowance. Both were true;
the unreadable reason is actionable. The existing handler test was updated to use a real PNG so it
keeps testing the cost gate, and three new assertions pin the new ordering down.

Tests: 79 new + handler 28 -> 40. **Full vision suite 292/292 green (was 252).** Rule 16 re-sweep:
26/27 repo suites green; `tests/forums-concierge.test.mjs` fails on a missing `@netlify/blobs`
install in this sandbox - verified identical on the unmodified parent branch, untouched by this
change.

Branch is committed in Ahmad's LOCAL repo (tip `0105193b`, parent `79bfe34f`). The sandbox has no
GitHub credential (re-proven: `git ls-remote` -> "could not read Username"), so the push is staged
as one click: **`_staged-cc-runs/stage-2-vision-cache-2026-08-04/AHMAD-PUSH-STAGE2-CACHE-2026-08-04.cmd`**
(refuses on main, re-runs all 12 vision suites before pushing, never merges, never deploys).
Bundle + patch beside it.

Never merged, never deployed, main untouched. Series-1 flywheel unaffected.

## 2026-08-04 — STAGE 2 BUILD READY FOR REVIEW - cc/stage-2-vision-offline-2026-08-04 (do not merge until Cowork clears)

**STAGE 2 BUILD READY FOR REVIEW — `cc/stage-2-vision-offline-2026-08-04` (do not merge until Cowork clears)**

Isolated branch off the Stage-2 lineage tip `cc/stage-2-vision-cache-2026-08-04` (`0105193b`, ADDENDUM 28).
Tip `9e00b0f6`. NOT merged, NOT deployed, `main` untouched, `cc/forums-mvp` and `cc/stage-2-vision-2026-07` untouched.

**What this slice closed.** The spec's cost clause says the `$0` offline KB stays the fallback. On the
image path it was not. Every route that could not produce a vision reading — **no `ARIA_VISION_MODEL`
on the deployment, which is the live site's state today and therefore 100% of real image drops** — plus
consent declined, allowance spent, global ceiling, per-IP throttle, oversized, unscrubbable, failed
paint, failed call — returned a flat abstain that **discarded evidence the user had already given us on
the same request**: the words they typed beside the screenshot (`body.text` was literally thrown away on
the image path) and the file's name. Those cost nothing, send nothing, and need no consent.

**Landed:** `netlify/functions/lib/vision-offline-fallback.mjs` (new, pure, offline, `$0`) decides what
counts as evidence and strips camera/OS filename noise (`Screenshot 2026-08-04 at 10.11.32.png`,
`IMG_1024.jpg`, `download (3).png` → nothing, deliberately) while keeping bugcheck underscores intact for
KB routing; all six image abstain sites in the handler now try the offline answer and fall through
unchanged when there is no evidence; the allowance refusal became `async` for the same reason (running out
of *paid* readings must not silence a `$0` answer); a caption now travels into the forums/escalation draft;
the widget (web + byte-identical Sentinel copy) gained an optional "in your own words" field, now sends the
file name, and **Cancel is no longer a dead end**. `package.json` — `vision:test` was silently missing
`vision-allowance` and `vision-result-cache`; three suites were outside the gate they were written for.

**Rule 14.** Every offline answer carries `imageRead: false`, `meta.visionUsed === false`, names its
evidence, and opens with "Nobody and nothing looked at your image — …" rendered **above** the diagnosis
(asserted by index, not by hope). A **filename-only match is hard-capped at `low`** however high it
scores, and the cap is disclosed. No evidence → the original abstain, unchanged. Consent is never
bypassed: a Sentinel capture without consent is still blocked, caption or not.

**Tests.** New suite `tests/vision-offline-fallback.test.mjs` — 101 assertions. Clean-room re-verification
from the committed branch tip: **13 vision suites, 393 + 121 = 514 assertions, exit 0** (was 12 files /
292). Rule 16 whole-repo sweep: **26/28 green**; `deploy-safety-denylist` (needs `.git`) and
`forums-concierge` (needs `@netlify/blobs`) fail **identically on the unmodified parent branch** in this
sandbox — verified this run by extracting the parent and re-running both. Extraction artifacts, not
regressions.

**Push — staged, not done (honest).** `git ls-remote https://github.com/...` → *"could not read Username
for 'https://github.com'"*. No code-hosting credential in this sandbox; nothing can be pushed to GitHub or
merged from here. The branch **is** committed into Ahmad's local repo. One click:

(refuses on `main`, refuses if the branch is missing, re-runs all 13 vision suites on the exact tree

`STAGE2-offline-fallback-2026-08-04.patch`.

## 2026-08-05 — STAGE 2 VISION BUILD (Series 2, parallel, branch-only)

**STAGE 2 BUILD READY FOR REVIEW — cc/stage-2-vision-2026-08-05 (do not merge until Cowork clears)**

Isolated branch off the Stage-2 lineage tip `cc/stage-2-vision-offline-2026-08-04` (`9e00b0f6`,
ADDENDUM 30). Tip `4d2cbb99`. NOT merged, NOT deployed, `main` untouched.

**What this slice closed.** Every Stage-2 answer — typed text, a dropped log, a PDF, the `$0`
offline image fallback, and the retrieval after a paid vision reading — is matched against the ARIA
KB corpus. That corpus was fetched from `https://iisupp.net/assets/aria-kb-chunks.json` on every
cold start, **with no timeout and no fallback**. One failing HTTP call therefore abstained all three
surfaces at once; a 1.4 MB round trip was paid for on every cold start to read a file sitting in
this same repository; a hanging request could eat the whole function budget (shared with the paid
vision call) and still return nothing. And `data.chunks || []` turned a 200-OK error page into an
**empty KB cached for an hour** that abstained on everything while looking healthy.

**Landed:** `netlify/functions/lib/vision-kb-source.mjs` (new, injectable, no import side effects) —
four routes in order: fresh memory cache → the bundled corpus on local disk (`$0`, no network,
cannot time out) → the network URL with a hard `AbortController` abort → the stale in-memory copy
rather than going dark; exhausted → throws and the caller abstains as before. A payload gate refuses
non-JSON / wrong-shape / empty / truncated / structurally-unrecognised corpora instead of caching
them. `netlify.toml` per-function `included_files` ships the corpus inside the vision function (the
pre-existing `_axis-state-full.json` include is repeated, not dropped). `meta.kb` now names the
source, article count, staleness and age on every response.

**Rule 14.** A stale serve is flagged `stale: true` **and** carries one honest sentence admitting a
recent article may be missing; healthy loads say nothing at all. No server file path is ever exposed.
Total failure still fails — the fallback chain is not a fabrication chain.

**Tests.** New suite `tests/vision-kb-source.test.mjs` — 56 assertions, including a fetch that never
resolves (asserting the abort signal is passed, that abort actually fired, and that it gave up in
under a second) and the 200-OK-error-page case. 7 new handler assertions, including one that kills
the KB host outright and proves a text question still answers and the network was never touched.
Vision suite: **14 files, exit 0** (was 13); clean-room re-verification from the committed tip
**456 `✓` + TAP assertions, exit 0**. Rule 16 whole-repo sweep: **36/40 green**; the four red
(`auto-fix-engine`, `forums-concierge`, `run-all-smoke`, `run-sentinel-kb-live-sample`) fail
**identically on the unmodified parent branch** in this sandbox — verified this run by extracting
the parent and re-running all four. Extraction artifacts, not regressions.

**Push — landed locally, GitHub staged (honest).** `git ls-remote https://github.com/...` →
*"could not read Username for 'https://github.com'"*. No code-hosting credential in this sandbox;
nothing can be pushed to GitHub or merged from here. The branch **is** committed into Ahmad's local
repo (`4d2cbb99`, pushed over the local path — refs only, `main` and the working tree untouched).
One click: `_staged-cc-runs/stage-2-vision-kb-source-2026-08-05/AHMAD-PUSH-STAGE2-KB-SOURCE-2026-08-05.cmd`
(refuses on `main`, refuses if the branch is missing, re-runs all 14 vision suites on the exact tree
before pushing, never merges, never deploys). Durable fallback beside it:
`STAGE2-kb-source-2026-08-05.bundle` (13 220 B, md5 `d091edd40c2e97ed1df03301c1a959e5`) +
`STAGE2-kb-source-2026-08-05.patch`.

**Still open for Cowork.** Live review with real screenshots before any merge — and now additionally:
on a deploy preview of this branch, confirm `meta.kb.source === 'bundled'` on a normal answer (only a
real deploy can prove Netlify honoured the bundling; the test asserts we requested it), and confirm
the function's cold-start time went down, not up.

## 2026-08-05 — STAGE 2 VISION BUILD (Series 2, parallel, branch-only)

**STAGE 2 BUILD READY FOR REVIEW — cc/stage-2-vision-consent-2026-08-05 (do not merge until Cowork clears)**

Isolated branch off the Stage-2 lineage tip `cc/stage-2-vision-2026-08-05` (`4d2cbb99`,
ADDENDUM 31). Tip `3af27715`. NOT merged, NOT deployed, `main` untouched (main moved to `ec9141b9`
under the Series-1 flywheel during this run; no collision — this lane touches none of those files).

**What this slice closed.** The server consent gate was a pure boolean: *is `screenCapture` /
`cloudProcessing` set to `true`?* and nothing else. `consent.ts` has been in the documented request
contract since the endpoint was written, and the web client has sent it since the consent dialog
was built — **no line of server code ever read it.** One approval therefore authorised a screen
capture and a paid third-party vision call for as long as anything replayed the request: a retry, a
restored tab, a resubmitted form, a queued job. The uncomfortable part is that we already knew the
rule — ARIA Sentinel's own `decideCapture()` has enforced a 2-minute TTL since the capture surface
was built ("Consent is NOT sticky"). The desktop app enforced it; the endpoint every surface
actually posts to did not, while describing its own gate as "explicit, fresh consent."

**Landed:** `netlify/functions/lib/vision-consent-freshness.mjs` (new, pure, injectable clock, no
I/O). Per-gate TTL — `screenCapture` pinned to Sentinel's `CONSENT_TTL_MS` with a parity test so
the two cannot drift; `cloudProcessing` deliberately longer so painting redaction boxes never
expires mid-edit. Env-tunable, with nonsense/zero/negative overrides ignored rather than obeyed, so
the gate cannot be switched off by a typo. Fails closed on missing, expired and future-dated
approvals, and distinguishes `missing` from `expired` so a user who *did* approve is not told
"Permission needed." The client now also sends `ageMs` (a `performance.now()` delta from when the
dialog was **shown**), which the server prefers — so a device a year out of date can still consent.
The disclosure states the approval is single-use and expiring, generated from the same TTL the gate
enforces so the words cannot drift from the rule. The blocked card renders "That approval expired"
with an **Approve again** button on the same image.

**Rule 14.** The timestamp is client-supplied. This makes "explicit, fresh consent" true for our
own surfaces and kills replay; it is **not** cryptographic proof — a modified client could assert a
fresh timestamp exactly as it could assert the boolean. Every response therefore ships
`consentEnforcement: 'client-asserted'`, the module says so in writing, and a test asserts it keeps
saying so. The real fix (a server-issued signed consent ticket) is named as the next slice, not
implied. No user-facing copy claims more than the mechanism delivers.

**Tests.** New suite `tests/vision-consent-freshness.test.mjs` — 50 assertions on a fixed clock,
including cross-module parity with Sentinel's `decideCapture()` on identical input. 12 new handler
assertions end-to-end (30-minute-old approval blocked, undated fails closed, future-dated cannot
mint permanent consent, wrong device clock still gets through, fresh approval still passes, raw
epoch never echoed back, $0 text carries no consent record). 12 existing test call sites now send
`ts` — what real clients already send; every original assertion unchanged and still passing.
Vision lane: **15 suites / 644 assertions / exit 0** (was 14 suites). Clean-room re-verification
from a fresh extraction of the committed tip: **644 assertions, exit 0**. Rule 16 whole-repo sweep:
**30 suites, 29 green**; the one red (`forums-concierge`) fails **identically on the unmodified
parent branch** — `Cannot find package '@netlify/blobs'`, no `node_modules` in this sandbox —
verified this run by extracting the parent and re-running it there. A dependency artifact, not a
regression.

**Push — landed locally, GitHub staged (honest).** `git ls-remote https://github.com/...` →
*"could not read Username for 'https://github.com'"*. No code-hosting credential in this sandbox;
nothing can be pushed to GitHub or merged from here. The branch **is** committed into Ahmad's local

## 2026-08-05 — STAGE 2 VISION BUILD (Series 2, parallel, branch-only)

**STAGE 2 BUILD READY FOR REVIEW — cc/stage-2-vision-ticket-2026-08-05 (do not merge until Cowork clears)**

Isolated branch off the Stage-2 lineage tip `cc/stage-2-vision-consent-2026-08-05` (`3af27715`).
Tip `f3f1e943`. NOT merged, NOT deployed, `main` untouched (`main` moved to `2411d0c0` under the
Series-1 flywheel during this run — no collision; this lane touches none of those files).

**What this slice closed.** Last run shipped server-side consent freshness and was explicit about
its ceiling: the timestamp it judged came from the CLIENT, so every response carried
`consentEnforcement: 'client-asserted'` and the real fix — a server-issued signed consent ticket —
was named as the next slice rather than implied. Two editable numbers in a request body were all
that stood between a replayed request and a screen capture plus a paid vision call. This is that
slice.

**Landed.** `netlify/functions/lib/vision-consent-ticket.mjs` (new, pure, injectable clock).
HMAC-SHA256 tickets minted by the server, bound to one gate, expiring on OUR clock, spent on first
use via a bounded burn list whose eviction drops the soonest-expiring entry — so a flood of fresh
ids cannot push out a still-live spent one. Constant-time signature comparison, length checked
first because a thrown `timingSafeEqual` is itself a timing signal. `vision-consent.mjs` prefers a
valid ticket over the client's timestamp and records `consentProof` per gate; the overall
enforcement label is the **weakest** proof in play, never the strongest. Handler gains
`{ action: 'consent-ticket' }` to mint, verifies and burns on the diagnose path, and now carries
the consent record on the image **abstain** response too — an abstain still consumed an approval,
and a capture may have happened before we concluded we could not read it. Client (web + the
byte-identical Sentinel vendor copy) requests a ticket when the dialog is *shown*, fire-and-forget
with a 4-second cap so a slow mint never holds a user's approval hostage, and the blocked card now
separates "already used" from "expired". `package.json`: `vision:test` had never registered
`vision-consent-freshness` (shipped last run) — registered, plus the new suite: **16 suites**.

## 2026-08-05 · STAGE 2 BUILD READY FOR REVIEW — cc/stage-2-vision-burnstore-2026-08-05 (do not merge until Cowork clears)

Series-2 Stage 2 (vision diagnosis), parallel lane, branch-only. Off the stage-2 lineage tip
`f3f1e943` (cc/stage-2-vision-ticket-2026-08-05) — deliberately NOT off today's `main`, which the
Series-1 flywheel is moving independently. Nothing merged, nothing deployed.

- **Slice:** the previous run's own named next step — the consent-ticket burn list moved from one
  function instance's memory to storage every instance can see. "Used once" now means once across
  the deployment instead of once per instance; the cold-instance replay hole that shipped as a
  written-down limitation is closed when a shared store is present.
- **Rule 14 shape:** three guarantees, each EARNED per request — `global-atomic` only when the
  store confirmed a conditional create, `global-best-effort` for read-then-write (race window
  named, not rounded up), `best-effort-in-process` when there is no shared store or it failed.
  Weakest-wins across gates. A deployment that CAN burn atomically but whose store failed on a
  request reports the weaker mode on THAT response. Fails open, and degrades the label when it does.
- **Ordering:** verify-then-burn. Only ids that already cleared signature, gate binding and expiry
  are spent — a forged copy of a real ticket cannot consume the real one. Pinned by a mutation.
- **Tests:** vision lane **17 suites, exit 0**. New `tests/vision-nonce-shared.test.mjs` (74
  assertions) + 8 new handler assertions (97 total). **Eleven mutations each turn the suites red**;
  restored code is green. Whole-repo sweep: 32 suites, 31 green, 1 red —
  `tests/forums-concierge.test.mjs`, missing `@netlify/blobs`, **fails identically on the parent
  branch** and is unrelated to this change (no node_modules in the sandbox).
- **Two real bugs were caught by these tests before they shipped:** a set-first probe read back its
  own write and called a first use a replay, and `nonceKey` let `..` through. Both fixed, both pinned.

**Still open for Cowork, unchanged and still the gate:**
1. Live review with real screenshots before any merge. Nothing here has been exercised on a deploy preview.
2. `@netlify/blobs` conditional-write behaviour (`set(..., { onlyIfNew: true }) → { modified }`) is
   proven only against a fake implementing that contract — the sandbox has no node_modules and no
   spend. If real Blobs behaves differently the code degrades to `global-best-effort` and says so,
   which is the safe direction, but it should be seen once on a preview.
3. Set `ARIA_VISION_CONSENT_SECRET` on a preview and confirm the response flips to `server-signed`.
4. Next slice, named not implied: expire burned ids in the shared store (a TTL sweep), so the
   nonce store cannot accumulate indefinitely on a long-lived deployment.

## 2026-08-06 — STAGE 2 BUILD READY FOR REVIEW — cc/stage-2-vision-2026-07-readquality (do not merge until Cowork clears)

Series-2 Stage-2 vision-diagnosis lane, parallel to the Series-1 flywheel. Branch-only.
Base = the prior Stage-2 chain tip (`cc/stage-2-vision-ttlsweep-2026-08-05`, 16 commits
off `origin/main`); this run adds the 17th. The branch name in the task file
(`cc/stage-2-vision-2026-07`) is already merged into main, so the new work is on
`cc/stage-2-vision-2026-07-readquality` rather than overwriting a landed ref.

**This slice: the image's own legibility now gates confidence.**
Confidence came only from KB retrieval score. On the image path the thing being scored is not
the user's evidence — it is Fable 5's *reading* of it, and that reading's quality was discarded.
A description that says "too blurry to read, possibly a driver warning" is dense with strong
retrieval tokens, so it produced a HIGH-confidence diagnosis and a one-click Fix resting on an
observation whose own author said it could not see the screen. That is the exact case the spec's
"low-confidence image → abstain (no fabrication)" test names.

- NEW `netlify/functions/lib/vision-read-quality.mjs`.
- Vision prompt now ends with `READ_CERTAINTY: high|medium|low` — readability, explicitly
  separated from confidence in the fix.
- We also judge the prose offline: illegibility admissions → LOW, hedging → MEDIUM, clean
  declarative prose → UNKNOWN (never promoted to high).
- Combine by WEAKEST; 'unknown' is an abstention that yields, never a vote. The module can only
  ever LOWER a confidence.
- LOW **revokes** the match → existing honest-fallback branch, plain-English reason, closest
  article preserved, no one-click Fix attached. MEDIUM ceilings the label at 'low'.
  HIGH/UNKNOWN change nothing but are still reported.
- False-positive guard: real "unreadable disk / OST Outlook cannot read" errors are NOT mistaken
  for a blurry photo (device vs picture nouns by distance; an exact tie resolves toward the read).
- Applies identically to a $0 cached replay — tested, since a cache that skipped the gate would
  re-open the hole.

**Tests:** `tests/vision-read-quality.test.mjs` (72) + `tests/vision-read-quality-e2e.test.mjs`
(28, handler end-to-end against a stubbed Anthropic endpoint — no network, no key, $0).
18 mutations against the new module → 18 killed, 0 survivors (the one initial survivor exposed a
real test gap and now has its own case). Vision lane 20 suites green. Whole repo 35 suites,
34 green, 1 red — `forums-concierge`, missing `@netlify/blobs`, fails identically on the
unmodified parent.

**Honest limits:** the gate reads LANGUAGE, not pixels — it cannot catch a blurry image the model
describes confidently and wrongly. Prompt compliance is unverified against a live Fable 5 call
(no key in this environment); a model that omits the marker degrades to 'unknown' (no cap) and
the offline prose check still applies. No live browser review with real screenshots yet — that is
Cowork's review step before any merge.

**Delivery:** commit `c4c5de1f` on `cc/stage-2-vision-2026-07-readquality` in the local repo.
GitHub push not possible — no credential in this environment (same refusal the Series-1 flywheel
reported this cycle). Bundle written for delivery:
`outputs/stage-2-vision-readquality-2026-08-06.bundle` (range `origin/main..HEAD`).

No merge, no deploy, no external send, no payment, no account creation.

## 2026-08-11 — STAGE 2 BUILD READY FOR REVIEW — cc/stage-2-vision-fixgate-2026-08-11 (do not merge until Cowork clears)

Series-2 Stage-2 vision-diagnosis lane, parallel to the Series-1 flywheel. Branch-only.
Base = the prior Stage-2 chain tip `c4c5de1` on `cc/stage-2-vision-2026-07-readquality`
(18 commits off `origin/main`); this run adds the 19th.

**This slice: the button is now gated by the same confidence as the sentence above it.**
The previous slice made an unreadable image revoke the DIAGNOSIS. It left the FIX alone, and the
two were allowed to disagree. A screenshot read at only *medium* certainty is ceilinged to 'low'
by `capByReadQuality` — deliberately, so it survives "as a lead rather than a verdict" — and the
handler then handed that article's TITLE to `matchFix`, which has never seen the confidence and
decides `oneClickEligible` from the recipe's risk colour alone. The user read "treat this as a
lead rather than a confirmed diagnosis" and, directly underneath it, was offered a one-click
repair that takes a restore point and changes the machine. The same hole existed with no image at
all: the abstain threshold is 8 and 'low' runs 8–11, so a match one token above abstaining
outright still produced a one-click Fix. And `matchFix` discarded how well *it* matched — a recipe
that hit an author-written trigger (+10) and one sharing a single ordinary word with the article
title (+1) came back identical and both eligible.

- NEW `netlify/functions/lib/vision-fix-confidence.mjs`. Three already-measured inputs that were
  being thrown away — diagnosis confidence (after every existing cap), recipe match strength,
  recipe risk — each map to a ceiling on how the fix may be OFFERED. Weakest ceiling wins.
- Offers: `one-click` | `confirm` | `steps-only` | `none`. high→one-click, medium→confirm,
  low→steps-only, abstain→none. keyword→one-click, pattern→confirm, title-word→steps-only.
  green/yellow→one-click, orange→confirm, red→steps-only, black→none.
- `matchFix` now reports `matchStrength` + `matchScore`, derived from the EVIDENCE not the total
  (twelve shared title words still score 12 and are still, honestly, a title-word match).
- Can only ever LOWER. A fix arriving `oneClickEligible:false` leaves false; unrecognised label →
  'low', unrecognised risk → 'orange', unmeasured strength → weakest. Silence never buys trust.
- Wired into BOTH fix-attachment paths, including the $0 offline-image fallback — our weakest
  evidence (no pixel read) and therefore the one that needed it most.
- Client (`assets/aria-vision-diagnose.js` + the Sentinel vendor copy, kept byte-identical):
  renders the offer. A withheld button no longer silently vanishes — the reason travels with it.
  `confirm` is a real two-press affordance, not decoration.
- One defect found and fixed by its own test: `weakestOffer` returned an unrecognised offer string
  verbatim instead of normalising to 'none' — a value no downstream consumer can compare against,
  and a comparison that silently fails is how a refusal turns back into permission.

**Tests:** `tests/vision-fix-confidence.test.mjs` (88) + `tests/vision-fix-confidence-e2e.test.mjs`
(30, full handler end-to-end against a stubbed Anthropic endpoint — no network, no key, $0).
The unit suite includes an exhaustive sweep over all 360 input combinations asserting the gate
never raises an offer, and checks the claim against the real recipe library rather than fixtures.
25 mutations against the two changed modules → 25 killed, 0 survivors. The first pass left 2
survivors, both exposing a real test gap (strength was asserted to *exist*, never to be *correct*);
that gap now has its own cases. Vision lane **22 suites green**, re-verified from the committed
tree rather than the working copy. Whole repo 37 suites, 36 green, 1 red — `forums-concierge`,
missing `@netlify/blobs`, fails identically on the unmodified parent.

**Honest limits:** the gate reasons about confidence and match provenance, not about whether the
recipe is *correct* — a high-confidence diagnosis matched to a genuinely wrong recipe still gets a
one-click, and only Cowork's live review with real screenshots can catch that. The 'confirm'
affordance is a client-side two-press; a caller supplying its own `opts.onFix` handler is
responsible for honouring `fix.offer`, and nothing forces it to. No live Fable 5 call was made
(no key in this environment). No live browser review yet — that is Cowork's step before any merge.

**Delivery:** commit `2ebae4b` on `cc/stage-2-vision-fixgate-2026-08-11`. NOT pushed: the mounted
`.git` refuses `unlink` in this environment (`Operation not permitted` on index.lock / loose
objects), so git cannot write a commit or accept a push through the mount at all — the commit was
made in a local clone. The GitHub credential is also absent, same refusal the Series-1 flywheel
reported. Bundle + patch written for delivery:
`outputs/stage-2-vision-fixgate-2026-08-11.bundle` (range `main..HEAD`, verified) and
`outputs/stage-2-vision-fixgate-2026-08-11.patch`.

No merge, no deploy, no external send, no payment, no account creation.

## COMPETITOR-DELTA 2026-08-11 (competitor-future-watch-weekly → CC/Codex task packet)

**Full evidence + every source URL:** `aria-vault/01_Frontal/IIS/Strategy-15-Years-Ahead.md` → §3e → *DELTA — 2026-08-11*.
**Loop-board suggestions:** `senior-director-state/loop-engineer/loop-board.md` → Watch Deltas → WD-10, WD-11, WD-12.
**Standing constraints for every slice below:** $0 · additive only (Rule 15 — nothing removed, renamed, or gutted) · every external figure carries a source URL or is cut (Rule 14) · branch `cc/watch-delta-2026-08-11`, never main · no deploy, no external send, no account creation, no payment · Netlify publish = Ahmad's one click · lead with the value the reader feels (Rule 17).

### WHAT CHANGED OUT THERE (3 items, dated and sourced)

1. **A Microsoft licensing cliff already landed and the GTA lane is silent on it.** Microsoft **Agent 365 went GA 2026-05-01**; **effective 2026-07-01, AI-agent security capabilities for Copilot Studio and Foundry agents require an Agent 365 license** — tenants without an eligible SKU **lost** those capabilities that day. Cost: **$15/user/mo standalone** (prereq: M365 E5, Defender+Purview Suite FLW, or **Business Premium**) or **$99/user/mo inside M365 E7**; agents themselves need no license; analysts say E7 is an enterprise play and the $15 standalone is the SMB path. Same date, **M365 pricing updates started 2026-07-01** (E5 $57→$60, O365 E3 +13%, Frontline +25–43%; **Business Premium flat at $22**; existing customers hold current pricing until first renewal after 2026-07-01). **No GTA MSP has published a free readiness check for any of this.**
2. **Verification became a billing primitive.** **Zendesk expanded outcome-based pricing in May 2026 and now bills only VERIFIED Resolutions** — confirmed by a **72-hour follow-up plus an LLM check** — with Assisted Escalations and Contained Resolutions billed at $0, dual verification of billed resolutions, and automatic overage billing above committed volume. Rates hold at ~$1.50 committed / ~$2.00 PAYG; the $0.40–$2.00 per-resolution band is unchanged. **The market has adopted our audit-chained honesty mechanic as a billing standard.**
3. **Freshness is now the measured #1 controllable AEO variable.** AirOps' 2026 State of AI Search Report (ChatGPT + Perplexity + Google AI Overview + Gemini): **83% of AI citations came from pages updated within 12 months, 60%+ within 6 months**; **AI Overview citations sourced from Google top-10 fell to 38% (from 76%)**; Princeton GEO lifts — quotes ~+41%, statistics ~+30%, citations ~+30%; AI-referred visitors convert **~4.4×** organic and spend **~68%** more time on site.

**No change:** GTA shortlist (Fusion, TUCU, ITBizTek, AYCE, MIT Consulting, Sun IT, IT-Solutions.ca) · GTA price band **$80–$250/user/mo** · Fusion's $180+/user, 1-hr critical SLA, 93% first-contact, CIS v8.1 · Atera Robin's **50%-in-90-days-or-fees-waived** guarantee + 72-hr PoC (only additive: 20+ languages, Salesforce, role-based AI Center permissions) · ServiceNow >90% autonomous / "99% faster." **No new MSP entrant found this run.**

### WHY IT MATTERS

- The Agent 365 event has the same shape as the 07-14 Copilot-oversharing wedge that worked for us — **but with a hard date and a dollar figure attached**, which converts better and is far easier to keep honest. It is unclaimed *right now* and the window closes the moment one competitor writes the article.
- Zendesk's Verified Resolutions removes the "nobody cares about verification" objection to our whole positioning and hands us a buyer question no GTA MSP can answer: *"which of your resolutions are verified, and how?"*
- The 08-04 freshness item (WD-08, ranked MEDIUM) is now backed by four-engine measurement. **It should outrank building any additional new page.** Un-refreshed answer pages silently lose their citation slot.

### SAFEST FIRST BUILD SLICE (do Slice 0 and Slice 1 first; the rest are queued behind them)

**Slice 0 — freshness cadence (smallest, safest, highest confidence).** Add a visible `Last verified: 2026-08-11` line to `managed-it-cost-toronto.html`, `aria-benchmark.html`, `copilot-oversharing-check.html`, plus `dateModified` in existing schema blocks. Copy/meta only — no layout change, no content removed. Then wire a monthly sourced-stat refresh checklist into this agent's weekly run. *Acceptance:* all three pages render unchanged apart from the new date line; schema validates; nothing removed.

**Slice 1 — `agent365-readiness-check.html` (new, additive page).** Client-side only, **no data leaves the browser, no email gate on the result**, answer-first first 200 words, FAQPage schema, every figure source-linked. Questions: do you run Copilot Studio / Foundry agents · did you lose agent-security capability on 2026-07-01 · which prerequisite SKU do you hold (E5 / Defender+Purview FLW / Business Premium) · $15 standalone vs $99 E7 arithmetic for your seat count · your renewal date vs the July 1 price change. Output: a plain-English result + an exportable checklist. **No IIS pricing, no offer block, no guarantee language on this page.**

**Slice 2 — "verified resolution" explainer**, added into `aria-benchmark.html` (additive section, existing content untouched): the four-way distinction **deflection vs remediation vs guarantee vs verified**, the Zendesk verification mechanic, the $0.40–$2.00 band, beside our honest **68.9% (self-test, n=45, not customer-validated)**. Category-factual, zero disparagement.

**Slice 3 — graduated-autonomy governance one-pager** (risk-tier table: auto for printer mapping / cache clear / disk cleanup; human-in-the-loop for firewall rules / permission grants / account changes) mapped to ARIA's **existing** kill-switch, approval gates and audit chain. Documents a capability we already have — no new claims.

**Slice 4 — third-party citation-surface playbook** (carry-over from WD-06/WD-07, still unbuilt). Draft the profile copy for CloudSecureTech, Clutch, **Cloudtango Top MSPs Canada 2026**, **mspdatabase.com Toronto**. Draft only — **account creation is Ahmad's one-click, no agent creates accounts.**

### APPROVAL GATES

- **Ahmad one-click:** Netlify publish of any page · every directory/review account creation · any commercial terms, guarantee, or outcome-pricing offer (none appear in these slices).
- **Codex review required:** Slice 1 (Microsoft licensing guidance is compliance-adjacent — verify every claim against the cited Microsoft Learn / licensing pages before it ships) and Slice 3 (autonomy/permission guidance).
- **Ahmad decision, staged not taken:** none this run requires money. Agent 365 at $15/user/mo is a *client-side* cost we explain, **not an IIS purchase** — we are not buying it.

### RISKS

- **Licensing content ages fast.** Microsoft dates and SKU prerequisites must be quoted with their source and their "as of" date, and re-verified in the monthly freshness pass. If a figure cannot be sourced to Microsoft's own pages, cut it (Rule 14).
- **Do not imply IIS resells or provisions Agent 365 licenses.** The page explains; it does not sell.
- **Do not compare our 68.9% against ServiceNow's 90% or Atera's 50% guarantee as like-for-like** — they measure different things; that is the entire point of the Slice 2 explainer.

## 2026-08-11 — STAGE 2 BUILD READY FOR REVIEW — cc/stage-2-vision-2026-08-11b (do not merge until Cowork clears)

Branch: `cc/stage-2-vision-2026-08-11b` (local ref in this repo; parent `cc/stage-2-vision-2026-08-11`).
Branch-only. main untouched. Nothing merged, nothing deployed, nothing sent externally.

This run's slice — **"the screen we send is the screen they picked."** A real Rule-14 defect found by
reading our own consent dialog against our own capture code: the dialog promised "ONE still picture of
the screen you choose" and its button read "Capture this screen once", while the code took `sources[0]`
and offered no choice at all. Harmless on one monitor; on a two- or three-screen desk the user approved a
sentence that was not true, and a screen they never looked at could be the one sent, unredacted, to a paid
cloud model. Both halves repaired: the choice is now real (pick by name; no default, no "primary wins";
declined picker / undisplayable dialog / monitor unplugged mid-flow are all refusals, never a substituted
screen), and the disclosure text is generated from the real situation so it never claims a choice that was
not offered and always names the screen about to be sent. Also retired the stale line saying pixels
"cannot be masked the way text can" — the paint-over pre-flight made that false. The audit now proves
which screen left, out of how many, with the physical display id and still zero image data. The widget
stopped answering every refusal with "needs your approval" and now names the real reason.

Files: `ARIA Sentinel/src/shared/vision-capture.mjs`, `ARIA Sentinel/src/main/main.mjs`,
`assets/aria-vision-diagnose.js` (+ byte-identical Sentinel vendor copy), `tests/vision-capture-source.test.mjs`.
`CAPTURE_DISCLOSURE` kept exported and unchanged for existing callers (Rule 15).

Tests: **209/209 green** across the whole vision suite (`node --test tests/vision-*.test.mjs`), including
the four the spec requires — known problem → correct diagnosis, low-confidence → abstain (no fabrication),
PII redaction, consent gate — plus 47 new assertions for the screen-choice slice.

HONEST CAVEATS FOR THE REVIEW (Rule 14):
1. The image path is tested from **simulated** Fable-5 vision text, never a live model call — a paid call
   in CI is neither free nor deterministic. **End-to-end correctness on real screenshots is unproven and
   is exactly what Cowork's live review must establish.** ARIA_VISION_MODEL is unset, so the cloud-vision
   path is dead until an operator sets it.
2. `tests/forums-concierge.test.mjs` fails in this sandbox on a missing optional `@netlify/blobs` package.
   Pre-existing, environmental, unrelated to this branch — it fails identically on the parent commit.
3. The branch could **not be pushed to origin (GitHub)**: this repo's `.git` carries a bad object under
   `refs/codex/turn-diffs/checkpoints/...`, which makes git refuse any object negotiation (`bad object`),
   and no push credentials exist in the run environment. The commit and its objects were written directly
   into this repo instead, so `git log cc/stage-2-vision-2026-08-11b` resolves normally. **The remote push
   is a one-click for Ahmad / an operator with creds; the corrupt codex ref should be looked at separately.**

Cowork: review live with real screenshots (multi-monitor case especially) before any merge.
[kb-growth-factory] 2026-08-11: +14 entries (windows-11-display, 40->54), 15/15 cells floor+depth met, 785 staged total, coverage 0% customer-facing (34th run unpromoted), staged for CC validation.

## 2026-08-11 — STAGE 2 BUILD READY FOR REVIEW — cc/stage-2-vision-reconcile-2026-08-11 (do not merge until Cowork clears)

Series-2 Stage-2 vision lane, parallel to the Series-1 flywheel. Branch-only. main untouched.
Nothing merged, nothing deployed, nothing sent, nothing paid for.

**FIRST — a delivery defect this run found and repaired, which a reviewer needs before anything else.**
The lane had quietly FORKED. Two runs on 2026-08-11 both started from `c4c5de1` and both logged
"STAGE 2 BUILD READY FOR REVIEW": `cc/stage-2-vision-2026-08-11b` (the screen we send is the screen
they picked) and `cc/stage-2-vision-fixgate-2026-08-11` (the button gated by the same confidence as
the sentence). **Only the first exists.** The second names a branch that does not resolve in this
repository and cites commit `2ebae4b`, which is unreachable from every ref we have — that run could
not write to the mounted `.git` at all and made its commit inside a throwaway clone. Merging the
branch that DOES exist would have silently dropped an entire slice, and the queue gave no sign of
it because both entries read as ready. This run re-applied the delivered patch onto the live tip
(commit `157aeb7`). It applied with no conflict — the two slices touch different regions of the two
client files — and the Sentinel vendor copy stays byte-identical. Called a re-application, not a
merge: the original commit object is gone, so its authorship cannot be preserved and saying
otherwise would be false.

**THIS RUN'S OWN SLICE — no one-click for a picture we never opened (commit `7914a56`).**
The recovered slice gated the fix button by confidence, match strength and recipe risk, and
described the $0 offline-image fallback as "our weakest evidence (no pixel read) and therefore the
one that needed it most". It was not gated there; it only inherited a cap that fires in one narrow
sub-case. When the picture cannot be read (cloud vision unconfigured, consent absent, allowance
spent, model unreachable) we answer from the words typed beside the image, say so plainly, and set
`imageRead:false` in the response. But `capOfflineConfidence` lowers confidence only when the
evidence was the FILENAME alone. Give it a real caption and the retriever scores that caption on
its own merits and returns 'high' — because as a sentence it deserves 'high'. Nothing downstream
knew the image had never been opened. Measured on the parent commit against the real KB and the
real recipe library:

    caption "outlook will not connect and keeps asking for my password" + an unread image
    -> l1-outlook-001-not-receiving-emails -> outlook-sendreceive-v1 -> offer 'one-click'

A run-it-now button, directly beneath our own sentence admitting we had not looked at the picture —
the same disagreement the last two slices were written to end, surviving one path further down.
Provenance is now the fourth ceiling and is STATED, not guessed: `true` (we read it) no effect,
`false` (image arrived, unread) ceiling 'confirm', `null` (not an image question) no effect. That
last line is the only place in the module where absence is not read as weakness, and it is safe
because it is not silence — both call sites state their case and a test asserts they do. 'confirm'
rather than 'steps-only' on purpose: the evidence is the same evidence a typed question gives us,
so what is owed is a deliberate second press that names the reason, not the removal of the fix
(Rule 15). No client change was needed — the recovered slice already renders `fix.offer`.

**Files:** `netlify/functions/lib/vision-fix-confidence.mjs`, `netlify/functions/aria-vision-diagnose.mjs`
(both `gateFix` call sites), `tests/vision-fix-evidence.test.mjs` (new), plus the seven files of the
recovered slice in the commit before it.

**Tests: vision lane 212/212 green** (`node --test tests/vision-*.test.mjs`), including the four the
spec requires — known problem → correct diagnosis · low-confidence → abstain, no fabrication · PII
redaction · consent gate — and all 9 capture-source assertions from the tip this sits on. New suite
is 45 assertions: the tri-state rule, an exhaustive sweep of 1440 combinations asserting provenance
can never RAISE an offer, the escape above re-run end to end against the real KB and real recipes,
and both handler call sites. **14 mutations → 14 killed, 0 survivors.** The first pass had 1
survivor: deleting the offline call site's argument entirely still passed, because the assertion
searched the whole file for the words and the response body a few lines above happens to contain
them. It now balances parentheses and checks each call site's own arguments. One existing assertion
updated, not weakened — the `publicFixGate` whitelist gained the two new declared fields; it failed
first, which is exactly why it exists.

**HONEST CAVEATS FOR THE REVIEW (Rule 14):**
1. The image path is still exercised from **simulated** Fable-5 vision text, never a live model
   call — a paid call in CI is neither free nor deterministic. **End-to-end correctness on real
   screenshots remains unproven and is exactly what Cowork's live review must establish.**
   `ARIA_VISION_MODEL` is unset, so the cloud-vision path is dead until an operator sets it.
2. The gate reasons about provenance and confidence, not about whether the recipe is CORRECT. A

   review with real screenshots catches that.

   this run by checking the parent out and re-running. Environmental, not caused by this branch.

   under `refs/codex/turn-diffs/checkpoints/...` which makes git refuse object negotiation, and
   unlink is denied through the mount. `git log cc/stage-2-vision-reconcile-2026-08-11` will NOT
   resolve here. No GitHub credential exists in the run environment either. **That corrupt codex ref
